bib.title: WizardLM: Empowering Large Pre-Trained Language Models to Follow Complex Instructions

read.skipped: Reference list and Appendix A-D prompt texts (deepening, concretizing, reasoning, complicate-input demos) only skimmed.

question: Can an LLM rewrite instructions into progressively harder and more diverse ones, so that fine-tuning on them beats human-written or self-instruct data?
hypothesis: Instruction data of higher, controlled complexity generated by an LLM improves instruction-following more than human-created or Self-Instruct data.
contributions: Evol-Instruct: automatic mass-production of open-domain instructions of varying difficulty with an LLM
WizardLM, which surpasses Alpaca and Vicuna on code, math, GPT-4 and human evaluations
A preliminary investigation showing instruction complexity matters for SFT

method.summary: Starting from Alpaca's 52k instructions, ChatGPT rewrites each instruction for 4 rounds with a randomly chosen in-depth (5 types) or in-breadth prompt, an eliminator filters failed evolutions, ChatGPT writes responses, and 70k random samples of the 250k merged data fine-tune LLaMA 13B.
method.task: supervised instruction fine-tuning with synthetic evolved instruction data

datasets.name: Alpaca (seed, plus 18k extra self-instruct for Alpaca baseline)
datasets.source: Taori et al. 2023, self-instruct from 175 seeds

datasets.name: Evol-Instruct data
datasets.source: generated by gpt-3.5-turbo (Azure) over M=4 rounds; ~52k per round C0-C4
datasets.preprocessing: initial and all-round data merged and shuffled; failed evolutions eliminated by 4 rules (no info gain judged by ChatGPT, 'sorry' with response <80 words, punctuation/stop-word-only response, copied prompt words); each evolution may add only 10 to 20 words

datasets.name: WizardEval
datasets.source: Github, ShareGPT, Twitter, Reddit, Discord; manually created

other.use: evolver, responder, difficulty judge, math judge

training.objective: supervised fine-tuning on instruction-response pairs with Vicuna chat prompt format
training.batch_size: 4 per GPU (8 GPUs, so inferred: 32 global)

inference.decoding: greedy search for WizardLM and baselines; max generation length 2048
inference.samples: 1 run per model, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: GSM8k 4-shot; Vicuna system prompt for fine-tuning

metrics.name: WizardEval
metrics.definition: GPT-4 judged score relative to ChatGPT (ChatGPT=100)

metrics.name: human pairwise win/tie/loss
metrics.definition: 10 annotators rank 4 shuffled responses (Alpaca, Vicuna, WizardLM, ChatGPT) on relevance, knowledge, reasoning, calculation, accuracy

eval.protocol: Blind pairwise human eval by 10 annotators with Kappa > 0.6; GPT-4 judges for AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, WizardEval; single final checkpoint, no seeds or significance tests.

prompts.text:
I want you act as a Prompt Rewriter.
Your objective is to rewrite a given prompt into a more complex version to make those famous AI systems (e.g., ChatGPT and GPT4) a bit harder to handle. But the rewritten prompt must be reasonable and must be understood and responded by humans.
Your rewriting cannot omit the non-text parts such as the table and code in #Given Prompt#:. Also, please do not omit the input in #Given Prompt#.
You SHOULD complicate the given prompt using the following method:
Please add one more constraints/requirements into #Given Prompt#
You should try your best not to make the #Rewritten Prompt# become verbose, #Rewritten Prompt# can only add 10 to 20 words into #Given Prompt#. '#Given Prompt#', '#Rewritten Prompt#', 'given prompt' and 'rewritten prompt' are not allowed to appear in #Rewritten Prompt#
#Given Prompt#:
{Here is instruction.}
#Rewritten Prompt#:

We would like you to evaluate and rate the difficulty and complexity of the following question. You should give an overall score on a scale of 1 to 10, where a higher score indicates higher difficulty and complexity. You must just give a score without any other reasons.
## Question:
{ Here is instruction. }
## Score:

Please judge whether the following question is a math problem, and only return True or False without providing any explanation.
Question: {instruction}

limits: Authors concede GPT-4 and human evaluation scale and reliability poorly, and the test set may not represent all scenarios.
Single run, final checkpoint, no seeds or significance; Table 4 shows epoch fluctuation (authors blame it for ShareGPT-seed GSM8k).
Code, weights, data links and LR schedule, warmup, precision not stated in the text.
Vicuna comparison uses 70k samples but Vicuna's data are multi-turn real conversations while Alpaca baseline was regenerated with ChatGPT responses.
Difficulty scores are ChatGPT-judged; used for analysis only, not to guide generation.
